import pytest
from target import url_basename

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url,expected",
    [
        # Empty input
        ("", ""),
        # No scheme, just domain
        ("example.com", ""),
        # Scheme without path
        ("http://example.com", ""),
        ("https://example.com", ""),
        # Scheme-less URL with domain and path
        ("//example.com/foo", "foo"),
        # Single path segment
        ("http://example.com/foo", "foo"),
        ("https://example.com/foo", "foo"),
        # Single path segment with trailing slash
        ("http://example.com/foo/", "foo"),
        # Single path segment with query
        ("http://example.com/foo?bar=baz", "foo"),
        # Single path segment with fragment
        ("http://example.com/foo#section", "foo"),
        # Two path segments
        ("http://example.com/a/b", "b"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b/", "b"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b?x=1", "b"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b#frag", "b"),
        # Multiple path segments (old regex should capture the last one)
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c", "c"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c/", "c"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c?x=1", "c"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c#frag", "c"),
        # Path segments containing dots and hyphens
        ("http://example.com/v1.2-beta/alpha-3", "alpha-3"),
        # URL with port number
        ("http://example.com:8080/path", "path"),
        # URL with userinfo
        ("http://user:pass@example.com/path", "path"),
        # URL with unusual but valid characters in path
        ("http://example.com/%E2%9C%93/✓", "✓"),
        # URL with encoded query characters in path
        ("http://example.com/a%2Fb/c", "c"),
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_expected_behavior(url, expected):
    """Ensure url_basename returns the expected basename for a variety of URLs."""
    assert url_basename(url) == expected


def test_url_basename_non_string_input():
    """Non‑string inputs should raise a TypeError (the original implementation expects a string)."""
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        url_basename(None)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        url_basename(123)   # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_url_basename_preserves_original_regex_logic():
    """
    Specifically test that URLs with more than two path segments still return the
    last segment, as the original regex allowed the optional part to consume
    slashes. This guards against the regression introduced by the pattern change.
    """
    url = "http://example.com/first/second/third/fourth"
    # Expected according to the original behaviour: the last segment 'fourth'
    assert url_basename(url) == "fourth"
